questions.question: Which of the following does not supply the diaphragm?
questions.explanation: The diaphragm is not supplied by a middle phrenic artery. The source lists its arterial supply as superior phrenic arteries, inferior phrenic arteries, musculophrenic arteries, pericardiophrenic arteries, and the lower five intercostal and subcostal arteries.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A cardiothoracic surgeon performing a heart transplant accidentally damages the right phrenic nerve. Where does this structure pass through?
questions.explanation: The right phrenic nerve passes through the central tendon of the diaphragm, either through the caval hiatus or immediately lateral to it. In the source figure this route is labeled 3. The other labeled structures are 1 - medial arcuate ligament, 2 - aortic opening, and 4 - esophageal opening. The left phrenic nerve passes through the muscular diaphragm anterior to the central tendon and is more anterior than the right. Phrenic-nerve injury during cardiothoracic surgery may cause diaphragmatic paralysis with elevation of the affected hemidiaphragm on chest radiograph.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A gastroenterologist is performing an esophagoscopy in a patient with severe acid reflux. At which level will he encounter its diaphragmatic constriction?
questions.explanation: The esophageal hiatus is at the T10 vertebral level and forms the diaphragmatic constriction of the esophagus. The source lists contents of the hiatus as the esophagus, vagal trunks, gastric nerves, esophageal branches of the left gastric vessels and some lymphatics. It also gives the normal esophageal constrictions measured from the upper incisors: cricopharyngeus at 15 cm, aortic arch at 22.5 cm, left bronchus at 27.5 cm and diaphragmatic opening at 37.5 cm.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A vascular surgeon is operating on a case of aortic dissection of the thoracic aorta. He suspects that the dissection has extended into the abdominal aorta, and approaches the aortic hiatus of the diaphragm to localize the extension. Which of the following structures will be present here?

options.text: Left gastric vein and thoracic duct
Right vagus nerve and thoracic duct
Left vagus nerve and thoracic duct

questions.explanation: The aortic hiatus transmits the thoracic aorta, azygos vein and thoracic duct. The source also reviews aortic dissection as an intimal tear with severe tearing interscapular pain; extension into the abdominal aorta can produce abdominal pain. CT or MRI can demonstrate the dissection, and management depends on classification and may include aggressive antihypertensive therapy or open/endovascular intervention.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A patient with advanced esophageal cancer in the lower third of the esophagus is undergoing transhiatal esophagectomy. The surgeon enlarges the esophageal hiatus with four fingers. All of the following structures are likely to be injured, except:
questions.explanation: The left phrenic nerve is least likely to be injured while enlarging the esophageal hiatus because it does not pass through a diaphragmatic opening; it traverses the muscular part of the diaphragm anterior to the central tendon. The esophageal hiatus contains the esophagus, vagal trunks, gastric nerves, branches of the left gastric vessels and some lymphatics. The source notes transhiatal/Orringer esophagectomy for lower-third esophageal carcinoma, with abdominal mobilization of the stomach/lower esophagus and cervical access to the upper esophagus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: All of the structures pass posterior to the crus of diaphragm except ____
questions.explanation: The greater splanchnic nerve does not pass posterior to the diaphragmatic crus; it pierces the crus to enter the abdomen. The aortic hiatus lies behind the crura and transmits the aorta, thoracic duct and azygos vein.
